Status: Wave 281 accepted (6.3): Class737 connect, disconnect and ack/nak paths

Method.evidence: The remaining Class737 handlers publish a message whose code is a readable MessageCode member, and the new --dump-constants command turns those numbers into the member names: T_Connect_ind = 133, T_Connect_con = 134, T_Disconnect_ind = 135, T_Disconnect_con = 136, T_Data_Connected_ind = 137, L_Data_req = 17, L_Data_ind = 41, and TPCI UnnumberedData/NumberedData/Connect/Disconnect/Ack/Nak/Invalid = 0/4/8/9/14/15/255 (which is exactly what ProcessAsync compares). So: smethod_1 publishes T_Connect_ind in CLOSED and opens to OPEN_IDLE (HandleConnectRequest); d publishes L_Data_req in CLOSED and moves to CONNECTING (HandleSendDataRequest); c publishes T_Connect_con when E19 is raised under IsConfirmed (HandleConnectConfirmed); smethod_6 publishes T_Disconnect_ind and closes (HandleDisconnectRequest); b publishes T_Disconnect_con and closes (HandleDisconnectConfirmed); smethod_2 stamps TPCI Ack 14 with L_Data_req (SendAck, plus T_Data_Connected_ind 137) and smethod_4 stamps TPCI Nak 15 with L_Data_req (SendNak).
Method.themes: New tool: NameCandidates --dump-constants <assembly-or-tree> [type-filter] prints every literal field with its value from the cached module bytes (de4dotEx f7e446a3), which is what made this wave decidable - the graph and the field review carry enum member names but not their constants, and the dispatcher compares numbers. Three Class737 rows stay unresolved with reasons: m publishes the same Ack frame as smethod_2 without the T_Data_Connected_ind step, a publishes T_Disconnect_con in the CLOSED state (the twin of b, which also closes), and smethod_10 publishes L_Data_req across four addressed-to-us triggers without a state change; telling each from its sibling needs the per-trigger decode rather than a placeholder name.
